# `Q-12-20` — Listing Record Path Names No Document

> An inline `contents:` record's `path:` has a document extension but
> names no document the project renders; the item keeps the link as
> written.

## What this means

An inline `contents:` record's `path:` can name a project document,
in which case the record's fields overlay that document's hydrated
item (its title, description, date, and so on fill in whatever the
record doesn't set):

```yaml
listing:
  contents:
    - title: Get started
      path: download.qmd
```

This warning fires when `path:` looks like it should name a document
— it has a Markdown/notebook extension (`.qmd`, `.md`, `.Rmd`,
`.ipynb`) — but resolves to no document the project actually renders.
The item still gets built, using only the record's own fields, and
the link is emitted exactly as written; it may point nowhere.

## Why this happens

- **A typo** in the path or file name.
- **The wrong directory.** `path:` resolves against the directory of
  the file the *listing* is written in, not the project root — a
  path written assuming project-root-relative resolution can miss.
- **The file exists but is excluded from rendering** — for example
  by `project.render`, or because its name or directory starts with
  `_` or `.`. Such a file is not a document `Q-12-20` can link to,
  even though it exists on disk.

## How to fix

- Correct the path. If the resolved path in the diagnostic names a
  same-named document elsewhere in the project, the message
  suggests it.
- Anchor the path at the project root with a leading `/` if it was
  written assuming a different base directory:

  ```yaml
  listing:
    contents:
      - title: Get started
        path: /docs/download.qmd
  ```

- If the record was never meant to link anywhere — just a card with
  its own title, description, and custom fields — drop `path:`
  entirely.
